text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
-Norway will probably sign an agreement to deliver 70 billion cubic meters of natural gas to the Czech Republic over a 20-year period. The deal would be worth 40 billion crowns.

-Electricity prices will remain high in the next years despite deregulation of the industry, according to a report by Coopers & Lybrand and Norwegian brokerhouse Fondspartner. The report concludes that electricity prices will remain at 0.23-0.24 crowns per kWh over the next years.
-A majority in parliament wants to alter legislation in order to increase competition in the pharmaceutical industry.
-Manager Tormod Hermansen at Norway's state-owned telecommunication company Telenor wants to list the company at the Oslo Stock Exchange next year.

-Borger Lenth, former head of Norway's second largest commercial bank, Christiania, says Norwegian authorities must allow banks to grow in order to be able to compete with foreign banks. Lenth also says the state should sell part of its 50 percent stake in the largest banks.
